evidence.quote: A structure as big as an arbor should be secured in the ground. There are a couple of ways to do this and you can find some links to great resources here http://www.iamahomemaker.com/simple-diy-arbor/

R1.reason: How the posts are secured in the ground is left to an external page; searched steps, materials, description for /anchor|concrete|bury|depth|gravel/i: only steps[0] "digging any holes or using any post anchors" (no method, depth or hardware). The frame itself can be built from the plan (posts braced, steps[2]-[3]), so Fix; likely because the link is offered as "resources".

R2.search: parts in steps[5],[6],[8],[9],[11],[12] (lower/top/middle 2x4 horizontals = 6x, verticals 4x, posts, beams, runners) all match cutList rows

R3.reason: all 5 rows used: horizontals 2+2+2 = 6x (steps[5],[6],[8]); verticals 2 per side = 4x (steps[11]); beams steps[9]; runners steps[12]; posts steps[2]

R4.basis: Kreg-corrected cut rows vs board materials (§9)

R5.reason: R5 precondition not met: 4 stock types (1x6, 4x4, 2x4, 1x2); steps not checked for per-part stock

R6.reason: sizes stated in steps: 2" nails (materials[7]) and 1" brad nails (materials[6]); other screw steps give no size; no conflicting sizes

evidence.quote: Using 2 of the 2x4x39.5" pieces, attach 16" high on either side of the arbor using pocket holes.
Attach the top horizontal support at the height of the lower mark you just made, using pocket holes.
making sure to keep them even on the top and bottom with the horizontal supports.

R10.arithmetic: lower mark = 16 + 74 - 5.5 = 84.5 (steps[6]). Verticals span top of upper support to bottom of lower support (steps[11]); with 3 1/2" 2x4s: 84.5-16 = 68.5; 84.5-12.5 = 72; 88-16 = 72; 88-12.5 = 75.5; none equals cutList[1] 71.5.
R10.reason: Which edge of the 3 1/2" support sits on the 16" mark and on the 84.5" mark is not stated; viewed images d8d602a2 (steps[5]) and 0dfba1ee (steps[6]) show no dimensions or edge reference, and the 71 1/2" verticals do not resolve it under any reading.

R11.note: 1 reference(s), each in a step with its own image

R8.reason: posts erected and braced (2-3), supports and beams on marks (4-9), braces removed (10) after the frame is tied together, verticals (11), runners (12), posts cut last (13)

evidence.quote: attach 16" high on either side of the arbor using pocket holes.

R9.reason: Pocket holes into 1 1/2" 2x4s (steps[5],[6],[8]); searched all steps/materials for a jig setting: none; viewed steps[5] image shows holes but no setting. Recorded only.

R14.reason: (a) beam 71 = 67 + 2 x 2" overhang (steps[9], description); 39.5 + 2 x 3.5 = 46.5 = description depth; counts match cut list. (b),(d) all parts installed, reaches finished arbor. (c) post anchors appear only as an alternative in steps[0] ("digging any holes or using any post anchors") and in a photo; no step instructs them - the missing ground-securing method and its hardware are scored once under R1.

gaps.what: Source text '4x4x8' is 8 feet; the cut-list length reads 8 (inches) — importer unit loss (cause import); materials[1] 4x4 96" x4 matches 8 ft

Ten 48" runners from materials[3] 'Board, 1x2 96"' qty 5: two 48" pieces from one 96" board need 96 + 1/8 kerf = 96 1/8", so each board yields one full 48" piece plus 47 7/8"; steps[12] lets the builder choose runner length

adjudication.note: R1, R10 upheld (likely); R14 anchors folded into R1 (post-securing method is the external link; steps never instruct anchors).
